newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco Chicago unleaded players on sidelines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco Chicago unleaded players on sidelines.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline differentials were talked modestly lower as trade opened Monday in Chicago with buyers and sellers remaining on the sidelines locked in a waiting game, traders said.

By late morning, no deals had been heard done in Chicago unleaded gasoline since Friday, when an Illinois judge cleared the way for Clark Refining and Marketing Co to restart two units at its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island refinery.
Discussion was muted by the annual American Petroleum Institute meeting, which drew several key players out of the market, traders in Chicago and Group Three said.

Chicago unleaded basis eased two cents a gallon on prompt and later November deliveries in Chicago on the Clark decision, which allowed the refiner to double gasoline production to 2 million gallons a day once the units were restarted.
Chicago unleaded was bid 6.75 cents a gallon, asked 7.25 cents over NYMEX December unleaded for prompt deliveries, and 4.75/5.25 cents over the print for later deliveries.
Group Three unleaded was steady at 4.0/4.25 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 1.50/1.75 cents over for later deliveries.
Prompt low sulphur diesel was steady at bids 3.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX December heating oil in Chicago and 3.75 cents over the print in Group Three, traders said
High sulphur diesel was talked 2.25/2.50 cents a gallon over the print in Chicago and eased to 1.75/2.0 cents over the print in Group Three.
Jet/kero was talked 3.50/3.75 cents a gallon over the print in Chicago and 2.75/3.0 cents over in Group Three.
